support_jay: Customer sees intermittent 401s from the streaming endpoint. Happening ~1/3 runs. Request IDs: req_9f1c2b, req_9f1c2c. Customer provided a curl repro — can someone help validate headers/auth and advise what to capture?

eng_sam: Can you paste the exact curl you used (redact token)? Also include the curl -v output and timestamps. If the token is right we should see auth checks in our logs.

support_jay: Pasting the repro I gave them (token redacted):

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "X-Request-Id: req_9f1c2b" \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-large","input":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams/generate
```

They say run 3x; about one attempt returns HTTP/1.1 401 and body `{"error":"invalid_token"}`. Timestamps from customer: 2026-03-17T22:18:12Z and 2026-03-17T22:19:05Z for two failures.

margo: Two quick things to try: add `Connection: keep-alive` explicitly and include `-v` so we can see response headers. Also include `-H 'Accept: text/event-stream'` (you already have it) and try with `--http2` to check if protocol differences matter. If you can, add an X-Request-Id that we can match to logs (you already did for req_9f1c2b).

support_jay: Tried the verbose run, here's the failing output snippet (redacted):

```

```

And our internal logs for req_9f1c2c show: `auth-check: token_expired, auth-service v2.4.1, checked_at=2026-03-17T22:18:12Z`

eng_sam: That log entry points to token expiry at the auth layer. Two possibilities: (1) the SDK the customer uses isn't refreshing tokens properly, or (2) there was a short auth-service regression around that time. margo, any infra events?

infra-bot: Auth service deploy at 2026-03-17T22:15:00Z had a partial feature toggle change; rollout was paused and a rollback started at 2026-03-17T22:16:30Z. Some auth-cache entries were invalidated during the window.

margo: Ah — that window matches. If the customer has long-lived token caches, they could get `invalid_token` for a short period even if the token looks valid. Support, please ask the customer to: 1) try again with a freshly minted token, 2) include `-v` output, and 3) if it fails attach the support debug bundle and include the X-Request-Id.\n
eng_sam: Also include this minimal repro we want them to run so we can eliminate SDK behavior:

```bash
# minimal streaming repro we want them to run 3x
curl -v -N --http2 \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <FRESH_TOKEN>" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \n  -H "X-Request-Id: <unique_req_id>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-large","input":"ping"}' \n  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams/generate
```

Please run it 3x within a minute and paste the `-v` output for any failures. If it fails, collect a debug bundle via the support tool and name it `debug_bundle:<unique_req_id>`.

support_jay: Sending these instructions to the customer now. I'll ask them to generate a new token and run the 3x repro and attach the `-v` output and debug bundle if it fails. Will update thread when they respond. :thumbsup:

margo: Thanks — if they come back with failures, ping me and include the `X-Request-Id` and the exact `Date` header from the response so we can correlate to auth-service traces.

support_jay: Will do. Marking follow-up for me in 30m.
